_description:
# The clock and its letters

The root daemon's `_clock` row moves a clock file every second; a register next to it sends letters every N cycles. Agents use tools `peek_clock` and `clock_register` instead (`aos/clock.json`).

clock.description: aos-clock: read the cycle number in FILE, write n+1, send the register's letters.

register.description: aos-clock-register: add, ls, rm entries that send a text to a mailbox every N cycles.

clock:
# aos-clock: one cycle forward

```sh
aos-clock clock && cat clock    # 1   (a missing FILE counts as 0)
aos-clock clock && cat clock    # 2
```

It prints nothing. You rarely run it by hand: the root daemon runs `aos-clock $AOS_DAEMON/clock` as its `_clock` row. After each cycle it sends the letters of `FILE_register.json` (see `register`). A letter that cannot be sent is one warning line (`aos-clock: warning: clock register entry w2: cannot send to .../nobox: MailboxMissing ...`); the clock still moves and exits 0. A FILE that is not a number = `ClockBad`, FILE untouched. No FILE = `ArgumentsBad`. `aos-clock register ARGS...` is `aos-clock-register ARGS...` (a clock file really named register: write `./register`).
register:
# aos-clock-register: letters every N cycles

```sh
aos-clock-register -d stacks/root add --every 10 --box stacks/root/procs/ann/queue ann-wake "Check data/ for new files."
aos-clock-register -d stacks/root ls        # ann-wake  10  procs/ann/queue  Check data/ for new files.
aos-clock-register -d stacks/root rm ann-wake
```

The clock: `-c FILE` > `-d D` (D/clock) > `$AOS_CLOCK`; none = `ClockMissing`, both = `ArgumentsBad`. The register is `CLOCK_register.json` next to it (`ls -j` shows it). An entry fires when the new cycle number divides by its EVERY (10, 20, 30 ...). The letter arrives as a user message `[aos] clock: cycle N. TEXT`. The same name = `EntryExists` (`--replace`); an unknown name in rm = `EntryMissing`. A box that is not a mailbox yet is a warning, added anyway. Every `check_every` cycles (default 100) entries whose box folder is gone are removed.
